limitations: Source-guided self-audit by the existing owner chat; not an independent or blind review.
No third-party application, production service, adversarial resource-exhaustion or hostile concurrent filesystem test.
Configured filter commands/programs are prerequisites for the Git execution issue; .gitattributes alone does not create a command in an ordinary clone.
Markdown rendering verified with locally available marked 17.0.5; no browser XSS or automatic image request established.
No dependency/advisory or credential-content scan; runtime dependencies are Python and Git.

findings.title: Git dirty-state inspection could execute configured target filters
evidence: At pre-fix commit 471a1087b5b28a77d813268ee723cf41a43c707c, collect invoked git status on the target.
A configured clean filter wrote a marker during baseline scan after a same-length tracked-file change. Process filters and nested repository filters were also reproduced.
The updated helper checks effective filter keys first and omits status when configured; it ignores submodule content when status is allowed.
attack_path: Repository contributor controls a program referenced by an already-configured Git filter, or an attacker supplies prepared local Git configuration.
A file requiring a content comparison is encountered during the scan dirty-state check.
Git invokes the configured filter with the scanner user privileges, violating the non-execution boundary.
counterevidence: Plain .gitattributes in a normal clone does not install a filter command.
The proof only created local disposable markers; no credentials, network or destructive commands were used.
findings.remediation: Skip Git status when effective clean/process filters exist; return unknown dirty state with a reason and ignore submodule content.

validation.result: Before: clean, process and nested filter execution reproduced. After: all three non-execution regression assertions pass; inventory and normal no-filter dirty-state controls remain functional.

findings.title: Imported report text could insert active links and forged Markdown headings
evidence: Backslash-prefixed brackets bypassed the previous escaping; bare URLs and embedded line breaks also remained active Markdown syntax.
Local marked 17.0.5 parsing of a crafted report produced three links and a forged heading before the fix.
Encoding punctuation as character entities and folding line breaks produced zero links/images and no forged heading after the fix.
attack_path: An imported report or retained source excerpt contributes attacker-controlled strings.
The user runs chatnoir render and later views the Markdown.
Incomplete escaping allows the data to become active links or forged report structure in a compatible viewer.
counterevidence: No browser code execution or automatic remote image request was established.
The validator is structural and does not authenticate a report; this fix protects rendering boundaries, not report truth.
findings.remediation: Treat imported fields as literal text by encoding ASCII punctuation and folding embedded line breaks before Markdown parsing.

validation.result: marked 17.0.5: before links=3, images=0, forged heading=true; after links=0, images=0, forged heading=false. Unit regressions for HTML, links, backslashes and newlines pass.
